questions.q: What is the rule for rounding up a decimal digit?
questions.a: If the digit to the right of the target place is 5, 6, 7, 8, or 9, you increase the target digit by one. A wrong answer here suggests the student has not memorized the threshold for rounding, confusing it with simple truncation.

questions.q: When rounding 5.62 to the nearest tenth, why do we ignore the 2?
questions.a: We ignore the 2 when deciding whether to round up because only the digit immediately to the right of the target place (the hundredths place) determines the rounding. A student who tries to include the 2 in the calculation shows they don't understand the "look-one-digit-right" rule.

questions.q: Round 7.84 to the nearest tenth. Show your steps.
questions.a: The answer is 7.8. Step 1: Identify the tenths place (8). Step 2: Look at the hundredths place (4). Step 3: Since 4 is less than 5, keep the 8 as is. A wrong answer suggests the student is rounding based on the magnitude of the whole number rather than the specific decimal place.

questions.q: Compare rounding 2.35 to 2.4 and rounding 2.32 to 2.3. What do they have in common?
questions.a: Both follow the rule of looking at the hundredths place to decide the tenths place. A student who cannot identify this commonality is likely guessing the answer rather than applying the standard algorithm.

questions.q: Is it ever correct to round 4.49 to 4.5 when rounding to one decimal place? Why?
questions.a: Yes, because the hundredths digit (9) is 5 or greater, which forces the tenths digit (4) to round up to 5. Students who argue this is incorrect likely fail to see how the "rounding up" rule works across boundaries.

questions.q: Create a decimal that, when rounded to the nearest tenth, becomes 5.5, but is not 5.5 itself.
questions.a: Examples like 5.46, 5.47, 5.54, or 5.52 are correct. An incorrect answer (like 5.6) shows a failure to understand the range of numbers that round to a specific value.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Rounding decimals is the process of ______ a number to a specific place value to make it easier to work with, by looking at the digit immediately to the right of the target place.
Fill in the blank: Imagine you are at a grocery store and a bag of apples costs ₹45.78, but you only have coins in increments of 10 paise or ______ rupees.
What is Rounding decimals? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Rounding decimals is the process of approximating a number to a specific place value to make it easier to work with, by looking at the digit immediately to the right of the target place.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Next, look at the digit to its immediate right (the hundredths digit, ______).
What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Rounding decimals?
questions.a: Students often try to round by looking at the very last digit in a long decimal (e.g., rounding 3.472 by looking at the 2 instead of the 7).

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to identify the target place value, check the "deciding" digit to the right, and correctly increase or keep the target digit to produce the rounded decimal.
